questions_and_answers.question_text: Which pattern is preferred in Chinese sentences expressing cause and result?
Why do English speakers find this pattern difficult?
Where does suǒyǐ always come in relation to the subject?
What other meaning may suǒyǐ have, and how is it pronounced then?
Write the Chinese for "I was very busy, so I didn't go."

answers.answer_text: Yīnwei wǒ hěn máng, suǒyǐ méi qù.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Are both yīnwei and suǒyǐ retained in Chinese?

answers.answer_text: Yes — often both are retained, whereas English would omit one of them.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "Because he is a good student, all the teachers like him."

answers.answer_text: Yīnwei tā shi hǎo xuésheng, suǒyǐ lǎoshī dōu xǐhuan ta.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "That's why you came here by plane."

answers.answer_text: Suǒyǐ nǐ shi zuò fēijī láide.

articles.text:
Notes on Additional Required Vocabulary

8.  huí guó          to return to one's native country
9.  huí jiā          to come/go home
10. huíqu            to go back
11. rènao            to be lively/bustling/noisy
12. yǒu yìsi         to be interesting
13. méi(yǒu) yìsi    to be uninteresting
14. suǒyǐ (suóyi)    therefore, so

Suǒyǐ (also pronounced suóyi) is the word "therefore," "so."

Wǒ hěn máng, suǒyǐ méi qù.       I was very busy, so I didn't go.

In Chinese sentences expressing cause and result, the pattern yīnwei... suǒyǐ... is preferred. English speakers often find difficulty in using this pattern because it sounds unnatural in English to say "Because I was very busy, so I didn't go." In English, either "because" or "so" would be omitted; but, in Chinese, both yīnwei and suǒyǐ are often retained.

Yīnwei wǒ hěn máng, suǒyǐ        I was very busy, so I didn't go.
méi qù.
Yīnwei tā shi hǎo xuésheng,      Because he is a good student, all
suǒyǐ lǎoshī dōu xǐhuan ta.      the teachers like him.
Yīnwei wǒ méiyou hùzhào,         I don't have a passport, so I can't
suǒyǐ xiànzài wǒ hái bù          leave yet.
néng líkāi.
Yīnwei wǒ yào dào Zhōngguo       I have to learn Chinese because
qù, suǒyǐ wǒ yào xué             I'm going to go to China.
Zhōngwén.
Yīnwei wǒ méiyou chē, suǒyǐ      I don't have a car, so I can't live
wǒ bù néng zhùde lí              too far away from school.
xuéxiào tài yuǎn.

Notice that suǒyǐ always precedes the subject of the sentence.

Suǒyǐ may also mean "that's why...": "That's why you came here by plane," Suǒyǐ nǐ shi zuò fēijī láide. When used this way, the word suǒyǐ is stressed.
